title: Which is greater, without working them out?
description: Fifty seven times thirty minus twenty and fifty seven times thirty one minus twenty are compared by looking at what changes. The second has one more lot of fifty seven. Keeko doubts that both are equal because both take away twenty.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare two expressions by finding the one thing that changes and what it adds up to. Watch for students who call them equal because a part looks the same on both sides.

source: Compare 57 × 30 − 20 and 57 × 31 − 20 without working them out, then check.
video_script.why: A learner compares two expressions by what changes, and then checks by working both out.
video_script.substitution: Replace fifty seven, thirty and twenty with any numbers where only one multiplier changes by one.
video_script.anchor: thirty lots of fifty seven and thirty one lots of fifty seven, each with twenty taken away
video_script.wrong_answer: the two are equal, since both take away twenty
video_script.wrong_move: sees the same take away 20 on both sides and calls the two expressions equal, so the extra lot of 57 is ignored
video_script.payoff_line: The first expression is less than the second.

final_answer.spoken: the first expression is less than the second

maths_rules: the slip: both take away 20 does not make them equal
video_script.design: Two blocks of fifty seven, thirty lots and thirty one lots, each with a small piece of twenty taken away. The extra lot is shaded.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; 57 × 30 − 20 and 57 × 31 − 20 written one above the other with a question mark between them

marks.h3: a question mark glows between them

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about comparing expressions.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>Fifty seven times thirty minus twenty, and fifty seven times thirty one minus twenty.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>We must compare them without working them out. Which one is greater?

beats.on_screen: the two expressions stay on the board and the question mark keeps glowing

marks.t1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a row of 30 lots of 57 above a row of 31 lots of 57

marks.g1: thirty lots of fifty seven are drawn
marks.g2: thirty one lots of fifty seven are drawn below

beats.colours: the extra lot in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Fifty seven times thirty means thirty lots of fifty seven.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Fifty seven times thirty one means thirty one lots of fifty seven.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>The second has one lot more.
<bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, fifty seven times thirty minus twenty, and fifty seven times thirty one minus twenty.

beats.on_screen: To find: which is greater, without working them out; then check

marks.fd1: the words which is greater and then check are written

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to compare them without working them out, and then check.

beats.on_screen: what changes: 30 becomes 31; what stays: × 57 and − 20

marks.s11: 30 and 31 are circled in different colours

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, find what changes.
The only change is thirty one in place of thirty.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>The fifty seven and the take away twenty stay the same.

beats.on_screen: 57 × 31 = 57 × 30 + 57, so the second is 57 more than the first

marks.s22: the words 57 more are written beside the second expression

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, see what the change adds.
Thirty one lots of fifty seven is thirty lots plus one more lot of fifty seven.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>The second expression is fifty seven more than the first.

beats.on_screen: the same − 20 on both sides leaves the difference unchanged

marks.s31: the − 20 is circled on both sides
marks.s32: the difference 57 stays after the − 20 is removed from both

narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, look at the take away twenty.
Both sides take away the same twenty, so it does not change which side is greater.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>The extra fifty seven decides it.

marks.a1: the sign is placed between the expressions and boxed
marks.a2: the values 1690 and 1747 are worked out as a check

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>The first expression is less than the second.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>To check, one thousand six hundred and ninety is less than one thousand seven hundred and forty seven.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>The two differ by fifty seven.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='k1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: both take away 20, so equal; it is struck out and the extra lot of 57 lights up

marks.k2: Keeko's bubble shows both take away 20, so equal
marks.k3: the extra lot of 57 lights up

narration: <bookmark mark='k2'/>Keeko thinks the two are equal, since both take away twenty.
<bookmark mark='k3'/>But thirty one lots of fifty seven is more than thirty lots.
<bookmark mark='k4'/>The same take away on both sides cannot hide the extra lot.
